name: WA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Larsen holds a D+12 district and is running for reelection
Larsen has raised $2.6 million to Edwin Feller's roughly $11,000
Prediction markets price Larsen's win chance around 96%
No public general-election polling is available for this race
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: Larsen is an incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by twelve points, has a two-hundred-fold fundraising advantage, and is priced near-certain to win by markets. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays at a large Democratic margin with wide uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late-breaking polling showing a single-digit race, or a surge of outside spending against Larsen, would be the first sign the fundamentals are wrong.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Washington's second district is a solidly Democratic seat, and Rick Larsen has held it for many years. He enters the general election with the advantages of incumbency, a district that favored Democrats by twelve points in recent baseline partisanship, and a dominant financial position: about $2.6 million raised and half a million on hand, against roughly $11,000 for Republican Edwin Feller. No outside groups have spent meaningfully against Larsen.

Prediction markets put Larsen's chances near 96 percent, and no public polls or expert ratings complicate that picture. The main caveat is the absence of polling, which keeps uncertainty wider than in a well-surveyed race. Even so, the combination of district lean, incumbency, and money makes an upset hard to see; the forecast calls this seat safely Democratic.
